stem: A developer builds a toggle with `role="switch"` and updates `aria-checked`. Which result shows that screen reader users receive the control's state correctly?

options.text: The screen reader announces the switch state.
options.rationale: The name, role, and state are exposed when the screen reader identifies the control as a switch and announces its current value.

options.text: The toggle shows a visible focus outline when reached with the Tab key.
options.rationale: A focus indicator shows where focus is, not whether the control is on or off.

options.text: The toggle's label uses the same font and size as the surrounding text.
options.rationale: Visual consistency does not tell assistive technology what the control is or what state it is in.

options.text: The page passes an automated scan for ARIA errors.
options.rationale: A clean automated scan does not prove that a state change is announced correctly.

explanation: For a custom control, assistive technology needs the name, role, and state. With `role="switch"` and `aria-checked`, a screen reader should announce a switch and say whether it is on or off, updating after each change. A focus ring, matching typography, or a clean scan does not confirm that the state is exposed.

references.title: W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices — Switch Pattern
